title: Perplexity Staircase
one_liner: Drag a model down the log-perplexity scale and watch capability thresholds unlock, from chat to millennium-prize math.
speaker: Peter Diamandis / Alex Wissner-Gross
context: OpenAI published a pre-training log-perplexity chart with capability thresholds. Alex explained perplexity as the number of equally likely next words, and read the flat stretch from GPT-4 to about GPT-5.2 as OpenAI losing, then regaining, its pre-training edge.
demo: A vertical slider sets log perplexity. A toy panel turns it into 'roughly N equally likely next words' and shows a sentence with that many candidate words fanning out. Threshold lines at the podcast's values light up as you pass them, and a toggle overlays a simulated plateau against a straight-line trend to show Alex's 'we're back' reading.
data_plan: Bundled threshold values stated on the podcast. The candidate-word fan is computed from the slider, assuming log base 2 as in Alex's 'bits' explanation. The plateau and trend curves are clearly labelled illustrative, not OpenAI data.
risks: OpenAI's actual chart wasn't shown in the transcript, so only three threshold values are known. The log base is assumed. Alex's 'back in 2002, 2003' is a slip for 2022–23, so don't reproduce it.
